strongest_objection: The design's entire content is a SECOND-ORDER forecast — a forecast of WHEN a first-order daily signal is switched on — and by the record's own numbers that input is below the detection floor inside any regime's lifetime, so "fast adaptation" is not a design choice but an impossibility at these SNRs. (a) IC units: at the memo's N_eff≈8 (`lore/fable_direction_memo_2026-09-03.md:162-167`) a per-date cross-sectional IC has SD≈0.35; a w-day window reads IC with SE 0.35/√w, so a 2σ detection of the 0.02-0.03 target IC needs w*≈1.5-3.4 years, while the record's regime labels last 8-14 months (`trader/config.py:71-79`) — the selector recognises a regime at about the moment it ends. (b) Sharpe units: 898's yearly cells have CI widths ≈4 (2024 net@8 +0.041 CI[−1.99,+2.10]; 2025 +0.663 CI[−1.21,+2.36]; 2026H1 −1.659 CI[−5.30,+0.95], `experiments/LEDGER.md:103`), i.e. SE≈1.0/yr, larger than any plausible true spread between lookback books — a trailing-1y selector chooses among noise draws. (c) Every in-repo adaptive re-estimation on the daily surface is measured non-positive: the equal-weight lookback ensemble (the variance-minimising best case for lookback adaptation) −0.16 (20-universe) / −0.09 (broad) FULL net@8 with turnover 0.162→0.177 (`runs/819_single_asset/PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md` sweep + lever table); the walk-forward per-regime-refit ridge on BTC daily lost to the frozen rule in 4/4 OOS regimes (net@21 −2.34/−2.41/−1.60/−2.09 vs TSMOM +0.29/+2.21/−0.23/−0.28, IC −0.04..+0.05, `runs/819_single_asset/RESULT.md` TEST B2); the imprint recipe refit per expanding fold posted OOS medians +0.31/+0.40/+0.41 while its floor swung 15× (+0.26..+3.90) — refitting tracked nothing (`LEDGER.md:99`); and any trailing-EV selector with a flat arm reproduces 887's attractor when all arms' trailing EV ≤0, which is the 2024-26 state of every measured arm (`LEDGER.md:97`; tactics panel :52-54). (d) Against the literal goalposts (`docs/pathway.md:9-21`: unseen years, net@21 ≥ +0.97, BEAR-positive, holds positions): on 2024-01→2026-06 the first-order term Σπ_kμ_k is ≈0 for every arm (PIT BULL24 net@21 −0.15, CHOP25 +0.02, `POWERED_RESULT.md` regime table; 898 by-year above), so the whole +0.97 must come from the timing covariance term over 2-3 yearly or ~30 monthly decisions — a term that is exactly zero if IC is zero and undetectable if IC is 0.02-0.03. The proposer concedes all of this (odds 1-2%); the record adds that its own closest precedents were omitted and that the memo (adopted as D79, `tasks/DECISIONS.md` D79 row) already set online/adaptive learning aside as at most a controller arm (memo :378-381).
amplifier_check: AMPLIFIER ONLY — it creates no information, and under the record's reading it is a lossy amplifier. The learned object in all three instantiations is a sequence θ_t of re-estimated weights / lookback choices / regime-similarity kernels. Its incremental information over a static estimator is exactly the time-variation of the conditional mean, Var(IC_t)·φ (persistence). That quantity is a property of the DATA and is read with LOWER variance by a direct estimator (by-year IC with placebo band; monthly-IC autocorrelation) than by the loop, because the loop adds (1) weight-estimation variance — the forecast-combination puzzle in its exact form: 819's EQUAL-weight lookback ensemble already lost −0.16/−0.09 to a single L, and an estimated-weight or winner-take-all selector has strictly more variance than equal weights; and (2) switch turnover priced at 21 bp/side: wandering to L=7 raises turnover 0.154→0.362/day (`RESULT.md` 1d table) ≈ +16%/yr fees ≈ −0.25 Sharpe at the book's ≈65% vol (11.65%/yr drag = 0.18 Sharpe on the PIT book, `POWERED_RESULT.md`). Under IC≈0 (the memo's load-bearing doubt) θ_t tracks noise draws and the loop's expected contribution is negative, ≈ −0.15..−0.3 relative to the frozen rule — the proposer's own estimate and the record's lever table agree. The only shapes in which the family shows a gain are forecasts by construction: X-Trend's +18.9% (Table 1, baseline Sharpe-loss DMN 2.27 → X-Trend-Q 2.70; zero-shot Table 2 TSMOM −0.26 vs X-Trend 0.47) is a forecaster trained on other assets' regimes at C(i)=0 (verified in the extracted full text, p.~5 "we set C(i)=0"), and the repo's one H2 "regime robustness" signal (831x/B, rule floor ≤0 in 2/4 windows while search reads +6..+10, `LEDGER.md:51`) is a TRUE-env lookahead — the value of seeing the future, not of adapting. Nothing in the family feeds a Monte Carlo search with information a closed-form selector lacks: a lookback selector with switching cost is a K=5 bandit solvable by Hedge or a ridge selector (tactics panel :132-135); Bella-as-world-model rollouts (the untested ansatz, `docs/findings/encoder_bella_class_closed.md:29`) carry no drift information beyond a forecaster (memo §5 :374-377). Verdict: the loop amplifies the targets it is given; the targets' existence is the question TASK_915 asks.

kill_experiment_critique: The experiment is honest about its expected outcome but its discriminating half is mis-aimed and under-powered, so as written it can only confirm the floor exists — it cannot measure Var(IC_t)·φ. (1) COMPONENT MISMATCH: arm (i)'s profit is the TIME-SERIES-momentum book's market-timing component (mean sign × market return — the short leg that made BEAR22 +1.095 vs long-flat −2.471, `LEDGER.md:103`), which a market-residual, cross-sectionally-demeaned target REMOVES by construction (memo :250-257 reports the market-factor timing arm separately, 'never pooled'). KILL-1 (cross-sectional IC inside the placebo band) can therefore fire while a lookback selector has real market-timing information, and vice versa; the IC/persistence read answers 915's question, not the selector's. The selector's discriminator must be in Sharpe units on the trend books themselves (per-year net@21 of each lookback book, autocorrelation of the yearly/half-yearly ranking, vs the random-selector null) — which arms B/C/D/N already produce; drop the claim that KILL-1 decides question (3) for arm (i). (2) POWER OF THE PERSISTENCE TEST, by the proposal's own numbers: at N_eff≈8, σ_date≈0.35, a 30-day monthly mean IC has SE 0.35/√30≈0.065; if IC_t has cross-month SD 0.03 (the design's own target amplitude), the signal share of monthly variance is 0.03²/(0.03²+0.065²)≈18%, so even perfect persistence φ=1 yields an observed lag-1 autocorrelation ≈0.18 against an SE of ≈1/√30≈0.18 over the 30-month binding window — t≈1, never ≥2. The SURVIVE clause 'monthly-IC lag-1..3 autocorrelation >0 at t≥2' is reachable only if the IC amplitude is ≳0.05 or N_eff ≳30-40 (at N_eff=40: σ_date 0.16, monthly SE 0.029, share ≈52%, t≈2.8 at φ=1). Pre-register this power curve as a function of the MEASURED σ_date and report 'unpowered' explicitly when it binds, otherwise a KILL-1 result will be read as 'no regime structure' when it means 'unmeasurable at this breadth'. (3) INSTRUMENT: a per-date Spearman IC of a TERNARY sign(30d) signal has near-zero cross-sectional dispersion on trending days (most signs equal) and is dominated by the few dissenters; use the continuous 30d return (rank) or the cross-sectionally demeaned signal, and state the tie-handling. (4) SELECTION INFLATION: B* = best of four designed selectors is compared to a null built for ONE random selector; pre-register B1 as primary and treat B2-B4 as secondary (or Bonferroni ×4), else the 'B* > null 95th percentile' clause is ~20% loose. (5) GOALPOSTS: add to every arm the BEAR22 (in-sample form check) and 2026H1 (unseen) net@21, terminal PV (875's positive-Sharpe-while-losing lesson, `LEDGER.md:99`), max drawdown, and the >95%-flat-days count; keep '>50% flat = FAIL'. (6) NULL ARM CONSTRUCTION: random-L-per-period selectors have DIFFERENT expected turnover from B (they switch every period); report the null at matched switch frequency or the cost term biases the comparison against N. (7) WINDOW/EPOCH: the trailing-1y read at the 2022-01-01 boundary uses BULL21 only; say so. Pin the PIT frame and epoch (post-E-d, `LEDGER.md:28-41`), name the daily-table end (898 ran to 2026-07-06), and inherit 915's 899-ingest precondition (`lore/notes_2026-09-02.md:113-114`) — the binding window's 2026H1 cells depend on it. (8) DUPLICATION/PLACEMENT: fold the IC/τ half into 915's SPEC as one statistic (915's grid is fixed at SPEC hash — if already hashed, it is a new row by the memo's own rule :329-330); place the selector half as a sub-arm of tactics row 1, whose oracle/hull/null arms it duplicates. (9) KNOB RULE: hysteresis 0.5 and cadence {yearly, monthly} are pre-registered parameters — any later tweak is a new row (`docs/pathway.md:30-31`), and no result here licenses a 'real adaptive row' unless C (the oracle) clears +0.97 on 2024-01→2026-06 AND B* beats the null — the oracle bound is the load-bearing output, so print it first. Cost estimate (≤0.5 CPU-day, zero GPU) is right; the 64 GB GPUs are irrelevant to every arm, as stated.
